common_name: Goldilocks Rocks Bidens (Semi-Double Golden Trailing Apache Beggarticks)

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated starts after all frost danger has passed and nights stay reliably above 50°F; this selection needs no pinching to fill in and begins its semi-double gold display within a couple of weeks of transplant.

directions: Goldilocks Rocks is a Proven Winners selection valued for its unusually tidy, mounding-to-trailing habit and semi-double golden-yellow blooms that hold their form better than single-flowered bidens types. Plant in a well-drained mix in full sun and let the soil surface dry slightly between waterings, since overly wet feet dull performance more than any other single factor. It is self-cleaning and needs no deadheading, making it a low-fuss filler for baskets and window boxes through the entire warm season. Feed containers lightly every few weeks with a balanced fertilizer to sustain the dense, continuous bloom.

common_name: Bee Happy Red Bidens (Bee Happy Series Red-Flowered Trailing Annual)

planting.note: Transplant rooted cuttings after the last frost into containers or beds in full sun; this series carries a naturally semi-upright, well-branched habit that fills baskets fast without heavy pinching.

directions: Bee Happy Red breaks from the usual bidens color palette with deep red ray florets tipped in golden amber, giving a warmer, two-toned look than the species' typical solid yellow. The series was bred for a more restrained, controllable habit than older bidens lines, so it needs less pinching or growth regulation to stay full and shapely in a pot. Grow in full sun with even moisture and light, regular feeding, and expect continuous bloom from spring planting straight through to frost. It is a strong pollinator draw, so site it where bees and butterflies visiting the flowers won't be a nuisance near doorways or seating areas.

common_name: Blazing Star Bidens (Timeless Collection Red-Centered Golden Trailing Annual)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in full sun after the last frost; Blazing Star's well-branched, upright-mounding growth fills out quickly and tolerates the heat of a Gulf South summer better than older bidens selections.

directions: Blazing Star is part of the Timeless Collection bred for earlier, heavier flowering, and it stands out among bidens for its bright red central star set against golden-yellow petals rather than the usual solid gold face. Give it full sun and well-drained potting mix, and let the top inch dry between waterings once established, since it handles heat and drought far better than excess moisture. Its upright-mounding habit holds shape well in mixed containers without sprawling as aggressively as trailing bidens types, making it a good mid-height thriller-adjacent choice rather than a pure spiller. Deadheading is unnecessary, but a light monthly feeding keeps the bicolor display dense from spring through hard frost.

common_name: Peter's Gold Carpet Bidens (Low-Trailing Honey-Yellow Groundcover Annual)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in well-drained soil or potting mix in full sun; this low, dense selection spreads sideways more than it climbs, so give it room to run along the ground or cascade over an edge.

directions: Peter's Gold Carpet is a shorter, more ground-hugging bidens selection than most trailing types, making it useful as a warm-season flowering groundcover along bed edges as well as a basket spiller. The honey-yellow, star-shaped flowers appear in quantity against fine, ferny foliage from late spring into mid-fall, and the plant is self-cleaning so spent blooms need no removal. It tolerates heat and dry spells well once rooted in, but responds to occasional light feeding with a fuller mat of foliage and more continuous bloom. Its more restrained vigor compared to larger bidens cultivars makes it a good choice for smaller pots where a rangier selection would quickly outgrow the container.

common_name: Solaire Yellow Bidens (Compact Semi-Trailing Container Series)

planting.note: Transplant after the last frost into full sun; Solaire Yellow's compact, dense growth suits small pots and combination plantings where a more rampant trailing bidens would overwhelm its neighbors.

directions: Solaire Yellow is bred for a shorter, denser mound than typical bidens, which keeps its bright gold daisy flowers held close over dark green, evergreen-textured foliage rather than sprawling into a loose trail. It suits rock gardens, border edges, and smaller hanging baskets equally well, and holds its compact form through the season with only minimal pinching. Grow in full sun with moderate, even moisture, letting the mix dry slightly between waterings once plants are established, since it is notably deer- and drought-tolerant. Deadheading is not required, and the plant continues flowering from summer into fall as long as it isn't allowed to sit in soggy soil.

common_name: Golden Goddess Bidens (Award of Garden Merit Vigorous Trailing Basket Selection)

planting.note: Plant vigorous, well-rooted starts after the last frost and give them ample room, since Golden Goddess builds a notably fuller, bulkier trailing mass than more compact bidens cultivars.

directions: Golden Goddess is a long-cultivated, exceptionally vigorous bidens selection recognized with the RHS Award of Garden Merit for reliable garden performance, producing an open, bulky mass of trailing stems better suited to large baskets and mixed containers than tight window boxes. The two-inch golden flowers are larger than many newer compact cultivars and are produced in steady succession over dense, ferny foliage from summer into fall. Because of its vigor, give it more room per plant than compact series bidens and be prepared to trim back overly long runners mid-season to keep the display tidy. It tolerates heat and dry soil well once established and is a strong draw for bees and butterflies.
